title: Expose distinct published engineering capabilities

statement: The system shall describe each published engineering capability with its purpose, invocation triggers, relevant exclusions, and behavioral owner so a participant can select work suited to the requested outcome before entering its detailed procedure.

what.problem: Similar capability names can cause a participant to choose review for authoring, implementation for an unsettled design, or factual research for an unresolved direction.
what.desired_outcome: The participant can distinguish supported capabilities and their relevant near misses from their public descriptions.

why.rationale: Selection must expose actual responsibility and side effects before work begins.

conditions: When discovering a capability or comparing neighboring capabilities for a requested task.

contexts: The selected capability path in the participant's project context.

how.approach: Present the current public name, purpose, triggers, important exclusions, specialist owner, and local handoff without requiring internal body headings or adapter-only metadata to make selection understandable.

how_much.scope: All currently published capabilities. Preserve the selected metadata and description constraints at their existing owner. Descriptions support selection but do not guarantee deterministic agent routing.

acceptance_criteria: A participant can distinguish a request to create an artifact, review it, execute implementation, investigate options, or resolve a factual uncertainty using the applicable capability descriptions.
Each published capability identifies one current behavioral owner and a justified recurring responsibility; a package folder alone is insufficient justification.
A description exposes important near misses and applicable scope without hidden mutation or handoff duties, historical rollout labels as runtime prerequisites, or synonym-only selection text.
Unsupported or ambiguous task fit is reported with the missing decision or relevant owner rather than silently selecting an unrelated capability.
